title: HIC Kitchen Mortar and Pestle for Grinding Spices and Herbs and Crushing Pills, Fine-White Porcelain
description:
About this item
HIC Kitchen’s Mortar and Pestle Set for grinding items into a fine paste or powder
Made from fine-white porcelain; complements any decor; mortar 2.75 x 1.5-inches; pestle 2.875-inches
Quickly grind and break down ingredients; speeds up food preparation with minimum effort
Make aromatic dry rubs, curry pastes, pestos, nut butters, and ground cinnamon, or grind peppercorns, prepare holistic remedies, crush pills, and more
Easy to use and clean; dishwasher safe for easy cleanup
reviews_5s:
I constantly use this mortar and pestal. It's perfect for grinding herbs for cooking. This size is much better than a smaller one.I would probably say this should be a 4.5 rating; but I don't get that option. I have a dog that needs Glucosamine-Chondroitin (G-C). She also needs some Ibuprofen, all on account of arthritis in her right (wrist) paw. I bought some "doggie" Ibuprofen that costs about 20 times as much as the normal stuff, from the Vet. Now, that Doggie G-C cost about 6 times as much as the human form of it that I buy for myself. But the main stuff I buy for myself has MSM in it. I called the supplier of that stuff I take, and they wouldn't tell me how much MSM is in it. They said it was a proprietary secret.

I looked up all the other people who sell the same strength medication, and ALL of them put 400mg of MSM in every pill and capsule they sell that contains the exact same amounts of G-C. For Dogs, one must regulate MSM very closely. It is guestimated that they can take up to about 2mg of MSM/kilogram body weight/per day with no problem. If dogs get too much MSM, they can develop cataracts in their eyes. But MSM is a very important thing when it comes to arthritis, because it stimulates the secretion of joint lubricants, in dogs and humans.

G-C provides the materials for the rebuilding of degraded (ground-down) bones in joints. MSM provides the lubricant to minimize the grinding and degradation. Ibuprofen takes away the inflammation that puts extra pressure on the joint in question. Such inflammation promotes the grinding and degradation. This is why I bought these mortars and pastels.

Now, I must say that veterinarians advise strongly against giving dogs human ibuprofen. Human ibuprofen focuses mostly on some type of inflammation designated as "Type 1." Arthritis in dogs occurs mainly with a type of inflammation designated as "Type 2." And there is NO doubt that giving too much human ibuprofen to a dog can lead to kidney and liver damage, even failure of one or both of these organs. But the research is there. Type 1, and Type 2, are not all that different. Doggie Ibuprofen focuses better on Type 2 than on Type 1, but it does both, as does human Ibuprofen.

So what I did was to maximize the G-C, keep the MSM (by combining other sources of G-C with more organic sources of pain relief with small doses of MSM), and I did that for a few months. I had to travel out of town recently. My dogs had plenty of food and water for 4 days. I came back, and my dog with the arthritis (Jynx) had hardly a limp at all. That was why I bought these things, along with a milligram scale to make sure I got the amounts right, at safe levels.

She gets the ground up powder in some soup I make for her, and for me. Whatever sort of Ibuprofen you give a dog should always be provided with food, so I dissolve it in the soup. She loves it, and she has nearly no limp at all, anymore. How ru going to force a dog to eat after you give it a pill? You have to give the medication in food, to start with.

These things work perfectly. I've never needed the biggest one, yet. Who knows?Use this whenever we make pesto. Great purchaseI am very happy with this purchase.

I wanted something to grind my Vit C tabs with, as the tabs were not easy to swallow, and given how important Vit C has become in the treatment of Covid-19, and having dug into the research myself, taking a fair amount daily preventively seems to be a no brainer.

Some ground breaking, interesting and very recent research has demonstrated there is a rapid transport system for Vit C directly from the stomach (if doses and stomach acidity are high enough), and the redox activity of ascorbic acid (vs none seen with the buffered form sodium ascorbate). It demonstrated very high doses being rapidly absorbed from the stomach on par with IV Iv adminustration of Vit C. So mixing the ground up Vit C tabs with something to take or drink seemed like the a smart plan of action.

I decided, after much looking, that a ceramic motar and pestle was the best way to go since steel can rust, and more porous materials can absorb odors and stains. I decided on this set due to added value of the various sizes included. I am quite happy with the quality and ease of use.

To initially break up the Vit C caplets I use the small mortar with the large pestle. They work very well together and make short work of it. Then, after getting it into a fairly fine-to-medium powder, I use the smaller pestle to finish getting the powder to a fine and uniform consistancy. This is all done very quickly. I then combine the powdered Vit C with something else to ingest it. I've been using a high quality extra virgin olive oil with a 'press date' (something hard to find, but tells you how fresh it really is), and when you add Vit C, wow the flavor pops! This has become part of my nutritional regime for staying well in these troubled times.

I've seen no staining or wearing to any pieces, and they are easy to clean. I am very pleased with this purchase. For around $15, this seems to be a very good value.I use it to crush medicine to make it easier to take.learning to cook with whole spices and these are great for pulverizing.Perfect size at perfect price!I do a lot of cooking and make all of my seasonings. The 4.5 inch set is perfect for this. I like that it is good and solid and fits nicely in the palm of my hand. I chose this one because the pestle is longer than some of the others (6"), making it very easy to grind up spices without hitting the sides with your hand. The outside is smooth and the inside part is rough, as is the end of the pestle. Maybe that is how they're all made, and it keeps the contents from sliding around. This is also a thick and durable mortar and pestle and I'm sure it is going to last a long time. I wasn't sure of the spout at first, but yes, it makes pouring the mix easily into a small bottle. It also looks very nice in my kitchen window. I am happy and satisfied with this choice and do recommend it to others without hesitation!I love this. It is the perfect small size for grinding my specialty course saltGranted, this is not a mortar & pestle set you'd find in a professional laboratory, but it very well could. It feels and acts like a much more expensive set. I'm assuming that most adults in the USA have taken chemistry classes, at least in high school, and have used a set very similar to this. If so, this will bring back memories - good or bad.

Rest assured that the inside of the mortar and outside of the pestle are properly rough - which is needed for easily grinding materials. If it were glossy, there would be no friction to hold your material from sliding about. The coarse texture is perfect and exactly what is needed.

The pestle fits in my hand well, and is very comfortable to use. I suspect it will fit even small hands.

The mortar is of adequate size (4" across measured on the outside) to handle most jobs in the kitchen, and sturdy enough for normal use. It must be noted that it is made of porcelain/ceramic, and can break if dropped on a hard floor or granite/ceramic tile counter. Under normal use, you should have no worries.

All in all, I'm very pleased and grateful Amazon made it available for purchase.
reviews_1s:
I bought these to replace a similar product that I broke crushing hazel nuts in. They appear to be very poor quality cheaply constructed garbage, which is where they are going. The bottom of the mortar is too thin, I suspect that the first time I try to crush anything in it, it will probably crack. The inside of the mortar is also has a flat bottom which vertical sides, like a ceramic cat bowl, rather than a true mortar, it is a joke, I don't even know how anyone can call this product a mortar, there is no way you could crush anything in this, without it bouncing out or sliding around, the manufacturer should be ashamed. The sides of the mortar are also too thin, and the dimensions depth verses diameter seem to be less than optimal as well, its overall appearance is of an object that was manufactured by someone looking to make a quick buck mass producing mortars and pestles, and who didn't take the time to note the fine design details of what makes these products functional. Sadly I haven't located anything better on amazon though so it looks like I am going to have to track down the company that sold me the first mortar and pestle years ago.Way smaller than expectedI've owned this for one month and am now buying a proper STONE mortar and pestle to replace this. I bought it to crush my daily thyroid pill and it seemed the perfect size for it. I thought I really liked it until the other day I noticed a shard of ceramic actually came off from the inside of the bowl. It was tiny and sharp and I counted my lucky stars that I didn't crush it with my pill or accidentally swallow that sharp piece whole. It made me worry that perhaps I've crushed other tiny pieces of the ceramic in the past and swallowed them, as the texture of the inside of the bowl has changed over the last month in addition to the spot where it chipped. Since then I've found out that a proper mortar and pestle is supposed to be made of stone so that this doesn't happen. I do not recommend this item as I believe it is a potential hazard. Please research and buy a proper stone mortar and pestle and keep yourself safe.Too smallI was truly disappointed. I should have paid closer attention to the reviews because the actual product you receive varies greatly. Mine seems sturdy enough. The pestle is shaped properly, but the mortar isn't, so they don't make full contact, which makes it extremely difficult to actually crush or mix anything.

Unlike sets I've used in the past, the bottom part of the pestle and the inside of the mortar don't have a ceramic coating. Dust really sticks to this. Also, that texture might work for DRY spices, but avoid anything with moisture.

I got this for mixing my own watercolor paints. The texture of this makes all the paint stick and soak in, making it impossible to remove and put into a paint pan, so all my paint was wasted down the drain.I purchased the 4.5" mortar and pestle because I wanted one slightly larger than the 4" set I got from another brand. The 4.5" one I received was smaller than the 4" one from another supplier. Yes, the HIC mortar did measure 4 1/2" if you measure the spout extension. The overall body was 4" in diameter and the inside diameter was 3 1/4". With other mortars I have owned the dimension advertised is typically the inner diameter since that is the dimension important to the grinding process. Including the spout in the overall measurement is misleading. Thus, I cannot recommend purchasing this brand due to the misleading description of the product.Left this review once already, but Amazon says it violates community standards. The listing says this thing is 4 inches wide, but it is only 2 1/2 inches wide. Plain and simple, not as described. If that violates community standards, maybe I should shop somewhere else.Too small to really work with. Chipped it straight away. Definitely wouldn’t buy again.I grind various size pills daily from 1/2 baby aspirin to large, hard caplets. I have used the standard marbel mortar & pestle for 10+ years but it can hurt your hands with the large pills and the small pills get lost in the bottom. I read all the reviews & selected these to grind the small pills. The pestles are too small for any of the mortar sizes. The large pestle might work in the smallest mortar but even that combination did not power the small pills well enough or without effort. This product increased my work effort. Maybe it could be used for a child trying help in the kitchen.
